items.title: How Much Skill Orchestration Can LLM Agents Compile Away? Execution-Grounded Specialization for Token-Efficient Skill Use
items.author: Jiayi Ni et al. (NVIDIA)
items.summary: The paper (SkillCache) compiles the orchestration inside a reusable skill into an executable fast path based on real executions, so the model does not re-interpret the skill on every call. It targets the token cost of bots that run the same skills over and over.

items.title: DISCERN: Preserve at Write, Resolve at Read for Persistent LLM-Agent Memory
items.author: Chirag Ahuja et al. (Amazon)
items.summary: On a 310-query enterprise sales-agent memory benchmark, the authors show plain retrieval already matches strong memory systems on recall; what remains unsolved is resolving which entity and which time-state a query means. They keep everything at write time and resolve at read time. Useful framing for bots whose memory holds conflicting facts.

items.title: MIRIX-2.0: Multi-Agent Memory System
items.author: Wei-Chieh Huang et al.
items.summary: MIRIX-2.0 is a multi-agent memory system designed to be accurate and efficient without training, and the authors report it is the most accurate of the compared systems on four of five benchmarks. Another open memory design to compare against.

items.title: Build agent harnesses for any LLM using the open-source OpenWorker Agent Harness SDK
items.author: Andrew Ng (The Batch, DeepLearning.AI)
items.summary: In The Batch on Nov 13, Andrew Ng introduced the OpenWorker Agent Harness SDK, an open-source, model-agnostic TypeScript SDK with tools, context management, guardrails, approvals, and durable sessions. A small, readable reference harness.

items.title: My biggest engineering work: building a harness from scratch
items.author: Manu Otel
items.summary: Manu Otel walks through a bounded streaming agent loop that builds context, calls the model, runs tools in parallel, returns results in call order, and enforces turn, time, and token limits. A first-hand account of the decisions inside a harness.

items.title: Security Bank trains more staff, develops AI agents
items.author: Philstar
items.summary: Philstar reports that Security Bank in the Philippines has trained more than 3,000 employees in agentic AI and that staff have built 3,100 small agents across business, operations, finance, and risk, with people keeping decisions that affect customers. A high count of staff-built agents at a mid-size bank.

items.title: Cisco, Goldman, and JPMorgan are reconsidering AI access at work
items.author: Business Insider
items.summary: Business Insider reports Goldman limits frontier-model access to work that needs it, Cisco is giving managers token budgets after unlimited use by coding teams, and JPMorgan capped some engineers' Claude Code spend at $2,000 a month; Rippling also has caps. Large firms are moving from open access to budgets.

items.title: Zurich reaches 93% Copilot adoption to better serve customers with Microsoft AI
items.author: Microsoft Customer Stories (Zurich North America)
items.summary: Zurich North America gave more than 10,000 employees Copilot and reports 93% active use, crediting role-based training, 1,200 prepared managers, and a peer Copilot Champions Network; it also cites 20% fewer service desk tickets. Another case where managers and champions drove adoption.

items.title: AI in UK financial services: looking beyond the numbers in the 2026 Bank of England and FCA survey
items.author: Freshfields
items.summary: Freshfields' Nov 16 read of the Bank of England and FCA survey says only about half of firms monitor AI after deployment, third-party AI makes up 53% of high-materiality systems, only 2% of agents have broad autonomy, and 57% rate cyber risk high or severe. A regulator dataset on where financial-firm AI governance is thin.

items.title: AI is boosting productivity gains as asset and wealth managers balance client priorities: MMI-Broadridge survey
items.author: Broadridge and Money Management Institute
items.summary: The 2026 MMI-Broadridge Pulse survey says 79% of firms using AI report efficiency gains, but only 45% of asset managers and 55% of wealth managers say formal AI training is widely available. Training still trails tool rollout in finance.

items.title: T. Rowe Price works with Anthropic to bring Claude to more of its investment process
items.author: T. Rowe Price
items.summary: T. Rowe Price is retiring its internal ChatTRP assistant and expanding Claude, including Claude Cowork for research and Claude Code for developers building investment tools. A large asset manager replacing a homegrown assistant with a vendor's.

items.title: All Code Is Slop (Except Mine)
items.author: Lauren Tan (xAI), AI Engineer CODE 2026
items.summary: Lauren Tan argues agent-written code can be trusted at high volume when constraints live in the codebase itself, through API design, lint rules, types, tests, and verification, instead of ever-growing AGENTS.md files; her team enforces directory boundaries with dependency checks and bans risky patterns in product code. A first-hand method from the team that builds Grok Bot.

items.title: feat(pstack): make Orchestrate agentic and delete the orch scripts (#1043)
items.author: cursor/plugins (pstack)
items.summary: The change replaced pstack's script-based Orchestrate with an agentic coordinator that spawns workers with Task, keeps state in a project tracker, and subscribes to PR and CI events, deleting the old orchestration scripts. It shipped in pstack 0.15.36 on Oct 27. A real switch from scripted to agent-led orchestration.

items.title: How to build an agent that builds the culture
items.author: Zach Bruggeman (Ramp), AI Engineer CODE 2026
items.summary: Zach Bruggeman says Ramp's internal coding agent Inspect keeps sessions public by default so engineers learn from each other's prompts and tools, and that about 75% of Ramp's code is now written and shipped through it. Shared sessions double as an adoption and training mechanism.

items.title: A New Age of Software Engineering
items.author: Walden Yan (Cognition), AI Engineer CODE 2026
items.summary: Walden Yan says Cognition replaced large teams with two- to three-person pods that own bug reports, QA, product, and their own Linear board, using swarms of agents for implementation, with work starting from a customer's bug video sent to Devin in Slack. A team structure built around agents.

items.title: Rethinking Claude Code best practices
items.author: Lydia Hallie (Anthropic), AI Engineer CODE 2026
items.summary: Lydia Hallie advises keeping CLAUDE.md to facts the model cannot infer, pruning it after model upgrades, using auto mode with deny rules for irreversible actions, and using hooks to lint after edits and block completion on failing tests (exit code 2, not 1). Specific, checkable settings for coding agents.

items.title: Build the company around the agent, not a pilot project
items.author: Quinn Slack (Amp), AI Engineer CODE 2026
items.summary: Quinn Slack said Amp deploys about 130 times a day with roughly ten minutes from push to production, and argued for organizing the company around the agent rather than running pilots. A data point on delivery speed when agents write most code.

items.title: JPMorganChase expands Claude Code to more employees
items.author: Anthropic
items.summary: Anthropic said on Nov 9 that JPMorganChase is extending Claude Code beyond engineers to product, infrastructure, risk and controls, and asset and wealth management teams, inside a controlled environment with staged access, model approvals, and human production gates. No headcount, cost, or productivity numbers were given. It is a large bank putting a coding agent in non-engineers' hands with explicit gates.

items.title: Tools, Trust, and Talent: how fund managers are putting Gen AI to work
items.author: Alternative Investment Management Association (AIMA)
items.summary: AIMA surveyed 104 fund managers with about $998 billion under management: 97% are implementing generative AI, mostly for research and memos, but only 31% use it in portfolio construction, and accuracy and data leakage are the main barriers. A peer benchmark for AI use at investment firms.

items.title: The finance professionals scared of AI might just be using the wrong tools
items.author: eFinancialCareers
items.summary: In a survey of about 2,500 finance professionals, eFinancialCareers found 39% of people using their employer's internal AI tools said they do not trust AI at all, against 27% of ChatGPT users and 29% of Claude users, citing hallucinations and slow verification. Some respondents bypass internal tools. A warning that a weak internal tool can hurt adoption.

items.title: NH NongHyup Bank unveils 10 AI agents to automate back-office work
items.author: Seoul Economic Daily
items.summary: NH NongHyup Bank picked 10 agent projects from 39 employee proposals, covering compliance, fraud and AML, recommendations, loan review, and remittance, and built prototypes with a vendor in about a month. Sourcing agent projects from staff proposals is a repeatable intake model.

items.title: Oxbow Partners and London Market Group launch report on the future of AI in insurance talent
items.author: London Market Group and Oxbow Partners
items.summary: Based on discussions with 20 senior insurance HR leaders, the Nov 12 report says AI will automate routine work and remove the groundwork junior staff learn from, so insurers need new apprenticeship and career models. It raises the junior-pipeline question that applies to any team leaning on agents.

items.title: Grok Bot on Mac can now use Messages, Mail, Notes, Reminders, Calendar, Location, and Contacts
items.author: Grok Bot (xAI) on X
items.summary: On Nov 12 xAI announced that Grok Bot for Mac can connect to Apple's Messages, Mail, Notes, Reminders, Calendar, Contacts, and Location, each enabled separately with a macOS permission prompt; Messages can read and send texts. It puts personal messaging inside a bot's reach, so the approval rules for sending matter more.

items.title: Alex Finn: Anthropic has the best model, Grok has the best harness (TWiAI 39)
items.author: This Week in AI with Jason Calacanis and Alex Finn
items.summary: On the episode, Alex Finn tested whether Grok Bot, Claude Duet, and ChatGPT Dots would send a $1,000 PayPal payment; he says only Grok Bot completed it, while the other two stopped on safety restrictions. Finn used it to argue Grok Bot has the stronger harness. It is a public test of how far each assistant will go with money.

items.title: Operate Claude Managed Agents inside your security perimeter
items.author: Anthropic
items.summary: Anthropic launched self-hosted Claude Managed Agents in private beta on Nov 12: customers run the agent server, database, loop, and sandbox workers in their own cloud or on-premises, while model calls go to Anthropic, Bedrock, Google, Microsoft, or their own gateway. It is the first major-vendor managed agent runtime you can keep inside your own perimeter.

items.title: Introducing AI Skills in Coworker: turn your best practices into reusable workflows
items.author: Salesforce
items.summary: Salesforce made AI Skills in Agentforce Coworker generally available on Nov 10: users write multi-step workflows in plain language, refine them in Skill Builder, and share them with chosen teammates, and skills run under each user's permissions with approval before record changes. It is the enterprise version of shared bot skills.

items.title: Artil Connect: let your agents message teammates and other agents
items.author: Artil (YC launch)
items.summary: Artil open-sourced Connect, an MIT-licensed self-hosted server that lets existing agents message each other and people over HTTP, Telegram, and Slack, connecting through plugins, a CLI, or MCP, with incoming messages able to trigger runs. It is plumbing for agent-to-agent handoffs across vendors.

items.title: Introducing Grok Bot 1.0
items.author: xAI
items.summary: xAI's 1.0 and 1.0.1 releases let bots on Team, Enterprise, and Ultra plans join Google Meet, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams calls from a link, answer in the meeting chat, and send a summary afterward; they also added Team Bots in Microsoft Teams and admin-controlled shared logins. Shared logins change whose account a team member's request runs through, which matters for approvals and audit.

items.title: Dylan Patel: 45% of SemiAnalysis AI spend now goes to persistent agents
items.author: Advance Intelligence, reporting Dylan Patel's post on X
items.summary: Dylan Patel said SemiAnalysis's AI spending went from zero to 45% persistent agents by the week ending Nov 8, mostly Perplexity Computer, which he said won on multi-model support and its harness; he criticized Claude Tags and OpenAI's Slack agent. It is a rare spend breakdown from a research firm running always-on agents.

items.title: Databricks launches new always-on Genie: autonomous AI for complex enterprise work
items.author: Databricks
items.summary: Databricks announced on Nov 11 an always-on Genie agent that runs in the background, manages long-running tasks, delegates to subagents, and alerts users through a priority inbox and email; it is coming to preview with no date or price. A data-platform vendor is now shipping the persistent-agent pattern inside the warehouse.

items.title: Fireflies.ai evolves from AI notetaker to AI teammate
items.author: Fireflies.ai
items.summary: Fireflies turned its notetaker Fred into a general AI teammate and added FredBots, no-code bots built in chat that keep context between runs and run on a schedule or after meetings, rolling out from a waitlist. Meeting-notes vendors are moving into the same recurring-bot space.

items.title: WorkflowArena: Benchmarking Executable Workflow Orchestration in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.author: Zheng Jiang et al.
items.summary: WorkflowArena is a benchmark of 145 long-horizon tasks that scores how well a model designs the executable workflow coordinating its own worker agents, separate from end-to-end task success. It measures the orchestration skill that matters when a lead agent spawns workers.

items.title: Cursor Projects is now multiplayer
items.author: Cursor
items.summary: Cursor made Projects multiplayer in beta on Nov 10: teammates share one task board and context while each keeps their own coordinator and worker agents, so agents can hand work across people. It is a shipped design for several people's agent swarms working one project.

items.title: Async subagents in Deep Agents
items.author: LangChain
items.summary: LangChain's Deep Agents added async subagents that run on an Agent Protocol server and return a task ID immediately, with tools to check, update, cancel, and list tasks and a choice to interrupt or queue follow-ups. A concrete API for a lead agent that keeps working while subagents run.

items.title: Swarms v17 InterLink: comms channels, phased fan-out workflows, and RouteHub
items.author: Swarms
items.summary: Swarms v17 adds PhasedFanOutWorkflow, where a lead agent writes a validated JSON plan, phases run in order with parallel steps, and for-each steps spawn one fresh worker per item, with caps on total and concurrent agents. An open-source implementation of fan-out with limits.

items.title: Unprompted coordination through shared memory in LLM agents: a locked two-implementation replication and extension
items.author: Pekka Abrahamsson et al. (GPT-Lab, Tampere University)
items.summary: The study tests whether agents start coordinating through shared state alone when nothing tells them other agents exist, using two independent implementations. Relevant to bots that share a workspace and memory without being told about each other.

items.title: Steering Emergent Behavior in Multi-Agent LLM Systems via Information Networks
items.author: Sepehr Ilami and Babak Heydari
items.summary: With ten identical agents playing repeated group games, the authors show that controlling who can observe whom, without touching payoffs or messages, changes collective outcomes. It treats visibility between agents as a design lever.

items.title: What breaks when you fan out Claude Code to multiple subagents
items.author: tomakl (Bits, Bugs, and Opinions)
items.summary: The post sorts fan-out failures into transient tool errors, ambiguous delegation, and latent failures that retries cannot fix, such as stale inherited context, conflicting outputs nobody reconciles, and actions taken before dependencies are ready. It recommends a reconciliation pass after fan-out. Practical failure modes for parallel agents.

items.title: Configuration-Based Sandbox Escape (CBSE) in AI coding tools
items.author: Cymulate
items.summary: Cymulate reports that coding agents can escape their sandbox when they write a configuration file the host later trusts; in Claude Code, a .claude/settings.json with a SessionStart hook ran silently on the next host launch, and similar paths were reported for Gemini CLI and Codex CLI. Agent-writable config is a host-execution path.

items.title: feat(installer): auto-approve Postman's Codex hook
items.author: Postman (postmanlabs/postman-plugin pull request)
items.summary: Postman's plugin installer wrote a trusted hash for its own Codex session-start hook, effectively approving its own hook after install; Postman later removed the behavior and added a revocation routine. A real example of a vendor tool granting itself trust inside a coding agent.

items.title: Devin Review 2.0
items.author: Cognition
items.summary: Cognition says Devin Review 2.0 typically costs $0.25 to $0.75 per pull request, about 80% of PRs cost under $1 including every push, and re-reviews only analyze what changed. A published per-PR cost figure for AI code review.

items.title: ViBench 2.0: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Software Building
items.author: Daniel Furman et al. (Replit)
items.summary: Replit's ViBench 2.0 has 17 full-stack web products built through successive feature requests to an agent, and Replit uses it to pick models for its platform. It evaluates the long, multi-request building that coding agents actually do.

items.title: AgentScript-Eval: Benchmarking LLMs and Agents for Code Generation in an Enterprise DSL
items.author: Dipin Khati et al. (Salesforce)
items.summary: Salesforce benchmarks models and agents on writing AgentScript, an enterprise domain-specific language for declaring agents, and studies how skill wording affects results. Relevant to any team asking agents to write in internal DSLs.

items.title: Launching the Langfuse AI Gateway
items.author: Langfuse
items.summary: Langfuse opened a public beta of an open-source gateway for OpenAI and Anthropic traffic with gateway keys, central provider credentials, model allowlists, and a trace for every request. One place to control and attribute model spend.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available
items.author: Google
items.summary: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon launched at introductory API prices of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through Nov 30, rising to $4 and $20 on Dec 1. A price change to plan for before it hits.

items.title: Client Zero: inside BCG's AI transformation
items.author: BCG
items.summary: BCG describes using itself as client zero, with a four-level AI Fluency Ladder from explorer to practitioner to automator to multiplier, the first two levels mandatory. BCG says nearly all staff reached level 1 within four months and more than 20% completed level 4. It is a ready-made fluency framework with completion numbers.

items.title: Commercial Bank of Dubai's AI-first banking push
items.author: Kazasec
items.summary: The report says Commercial Bank of Dubai has 92% Microsoft Copilot adoption among employees and an internal tool called Merlin that analyzes financial information and drafts credit proposals, with staff keeping the final decision. An adoption figure plus a specific credit workflow from a regional bank.

items.title: DFSA AI Survey 2026: AI adoption among DIFC financial services firms has more than doubled since 2024
items.author: Dubai Financial Services Authority
items.summary: The DFSA's Nov 2 survey says 71% of DIFC-authorized firms use AI, up from 33% in 2024; 53% are exploring or piloting agents but only 14% have deployed them, and 61% of adopters have governance frameworks. A regulator's view of where financial firms actually are on agents.

items.title: How Huntington is turning employees into AI enthusiasts
items.author: American Banker
items.summary: Huntington Bank runs two-day AI hackathons whose projects often go to production, ideathons that pair business and technology staff to pitch executives, and a Day of the Dead session where employees present failed projects and lessons. It is a set of adoption tactics that reward experimentation, including failure.

items.title: How Salesforce scaled engineering AI adoption without stifling innovation
items.author: Salesforce Engineering
items.summary: Salesforce describes embedding AI champions in scrum teams across about 500 engineers, who brought guidance into teams, fed problems back to an AI steering committee, and met weekly to demo new capabilities. It is a champions model for engineering teams that keeps team autonomy.

items.title: Grok Bot can join company Tailscale tailnets
items.author: Cursor plugins (Tailscale plugin README)
items.summary: As of Nov 10, a team admin can let Grok Bot join a company Tailscale tailnet so bots reach private MCP servers and internal tools; members authenticate their own bot device, which carries a custom:grokbot posture attribute that tailnet policy can restrict. It is the sanctioned route for bots to reach private services without opening them to the internet.

items.title: Musk: Grok 4.8 finishes pretraining, soft rollout to Bot users this week
items.author: PANews, reporting Elon Musk's posts
items.summary: Elon Musk said Grok 4.8 had finished pretraining, was in reinforcement learning, and would start a small rollout to Grok Bot users that week. No eligibility rules or pricing were given. A model change under running bots can shift behavior and token use.

items.title: Meet Nod: a standalone personal agent from n8n Labs that runs on your computer
items.author: n8n
items.summary: n8n Labs released Nod, a free, open-source personal agent with its own Linux workspace and browser that connects to Gmail, Slack, Notion, and websites, uses the model provider you choose, and asks before consequential actions. Another self-hosted assistant built on the same pattern as Grok Bot.

items.title: Vorflux AutoBots: 24/7 coworkers that live in Slack
items.author: Vorflux
items.summary: Vorflux 2.0 adds AutoBots, persistent agents hired from a catalog into dedicated Slack channels for standing roles like on-call triage, cloud-cost work, and release management, each with its own daily or weekly budget and approvals in Slack. Per-bot budgets are a concrete answer to bot cost control.

items.title: What's new in OpenBot 1.0
items.author: CopilotKit
items.summary: CopilotKit shipped OpenBot 1.0, an MIT-licensed, self-hostable AI-coworker workspace that runs locally or on your own Kubernetes cluster from one Helm chart, with your own models and built-in approval controls. It is the most enterprise-oriented of the open-source Grok Bot alternatives so far.

items.title: Grok Bot on The X Subscription: one shared weekly usage pool
items.author: xAI docs
items.summary: xAI's docs say Grok Bot has no separate quota on The X Subscription: it draws from one weekly pool shared with Grok and Cursor for each paid seat, with prepaid credits past the pool. Every bot and routine on a seat competes for the same allowance.

items.title: Introducing AlphaProof Code: verifying complex software at depth
items.author: Google DeepMind
items.summary: DeepMind's AlphaProof Code has people approve Lean specifications and agents generate proofs that Lean's kernel checks; DeepMind used it to verify libsignal compiled to AArch64 machine code, proving PQXDH and Triple Ratchet properties such as forward secrecy. The Lean development is public. It is agent-written proofs reaching shipped cryptographic code at the machine-code level.

items.title: PDD Kit (Proof-Driven Development)
items.author: GitHub Next and Microsoft Research
items.summary: PDD Kit turns approved feature intent into Verus specifications and proves that agent-written Rust satisfies them for every modeled input, while parts that cannot be proved, like UI and I/O, are tested and labeled as empirical evidence. It is a workflow for asking a coding agent for proof instead of review.

items.title: Progress on provable inference for large language models (FlashProve)
items.author: Anthropic
items.summary: Anthropic's open-source FlashProve lets a provider commit to model weights and produce a proof that given outputs came from that model, verifiable without the weights; a Lean 4 formalization machine-checks the verifier's soundness, while the fast production verifier is tested against it, not proved. It is formal methods applied to checking which model actually answered.

items.title: Lean now ships with verified kernels
items.author: Leonardo de Moura
items.summary: Leonardo de Moura announced that Lean 4.35 includes lake check, which re-checks a project's export in a sandbox, and a paranoid mode that passes only if several independent kernels, including lean4lean and nanoda, all accept it. It shrinks how much you have to trust when agents write the proofs.

items.title: Specula: Scaling formal specifications for autonomous model checking of system code
items.author: Qian Cheng et al.
items.summary: Specula uses coding agents to write TLA+ specifications, including invariants and implementation models, for large system code and then model-checks them to find bugs, fully autonomously. A push-button route from code to TLA+ checking.

items.title: Property-based testing for agent-written code
items.author: Developer Toolkit
items.summary: The guide recommends writing property tests from approved spec invariants before implementation, then locking them so the agent cannot edit them, through agent settings, CODEOWNERS, and running the decisive tests from protected base-branch files. A practical way to keep the test oracle out of the agent's reach.

items.title: Brian Armstrong on running lead agents under a chief-of-staff agent
items.author: Brian Armstrong (Coinbase) on X
items.summary: On Nov 7 Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong described a chief-of-staff agent that oversees always-on lead agents, each managing sub-agents that write code, test it, and chase reviews. Every decision and review lands in one prioritized queue in a local web app with screenshots and demos, which he clears in batches. It is a public example from a crypto company's CEO of the one-queue pattern for supervising many agents.

items.title: Import from other agents: hermes migrate grok-bot
items.author: Nous Research (Hermes Agent docs)
items.summary: Hermes Agent added an importer: hermes migrate grok-bot installs a plugin, has each bot write an export file, and brings its skills, memories, and routines across, with routines arriving as paused cron jobs. It shows what a bot's portable state looks like and gives an exit path if you ever leave Grok Bot.

items.title: Grok Bot changelog: 0.79.2 and 0.79.3
items.author: xAI
items.summary: The 0.79.2 release added a warning when a web page contains instructions hidden for AI agents, saying the bot found them and did not follow them, along with Tailscale and SSH support; 0.79.3 added shared Page theme switching and fixes. The hidden-instructions warning is a visible prompt-injection defense for bots that browse.

items.title: Leaked: xAI building Grok Academy at learn.grok.com
items.author: AGI Hunt
items.summary: AGI Hunt reported on Nov 10 that xAI is building an official Grok Academy at learn.grok.com with 15 courses on AI fluency, Grok Bot, and Grok Build and planned completion certificates; the site was not yet open. If it ships, it is ready-made training material for rolling bots out to a team.

items.title: Qianwen Office 2.0: proactive and collaborative, toward the Team Agent era
items.author: Alibaba Qianwen Office (QwenWork)
items.summary: Alibaba launched Qianwen Office 2.0 on Nov 9, a team agent that shares a workspace with a group, reads linked DingTalk chats, documents, spreadsheets, and meeting notes, summarizes progress, assigns tasks, and follows up, with event-triggered tasks. It is a large vendor shipping one shared agent per team instead of one per person.

items.title: Claude Connect: a Grok Bot template that forwards tasks to Claude
items.author: Martin Gontovnikas (@mgonto)
items.summary: On Nov 8 Martin Gontovnikas published a Grok Bot template that sends tasks to Claude through the owner's own Claude subscription and returns the answer unchanged, with guided login, read-only connectors, and answer comparisons. It is a working example of one bot acting as a proxy to another vendor's model.

items.title: The components of agent memory
items.author: Anthropic
items.summary: Anthropic lays out memory as layers: raw transcripts, notes written when something seems important, linked wiki-style structures, and a small context block loaded at each session start, plus offline "dreaming" that corrects stale notes and promotes what matters. A clear model for designing bot memory.

items.title: Anatomy of a frontier harness: side models, lifecycle hooks, and durable time
items.author: Julien Hovan
items.summary: Julien Hovan argues that multi-day coding agents need a fast side model for recall and supervision, hooks that save raw session evidence before memory is consolidated, and three ways to wait: synchronous commands, background monitors, and scheduled wakeups that resume a session hours or days later. A practitioner's design notes for long-running agents.

items.title: Delivered, Not Used: Evaluating Agent Memory at Its Point of Use
items.author: Changran Xu et al.
items.summary: MemUse checks, in recorded runs, whether an agent actually used a memory that was delivered to it and what followed, instead of scoring retrieval quality. It is a way to test whether bot memory changes behavior.

items.title: MEMOIR: A Training-Free Memory Lifecycle for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.author: Mayank Anand et al.
items.summary: The paper argues that writing memories with fixed importance scores lets consolidation destroy evidence later queries need, and revises memories based on how they are used. Relevant to bots that summarize and prune their own memory.

items.title: Reglos: A Self-Evolving Personal Memory Agent with Recursive Self-Improvement
items.author: Sen Yang et al.
items.summary: Reglos lets a coding agent patch the harness that turns a personal agent's memory into context, and guards against patches that only fix the failures they were tested on. A study of safe self-modification for personal agents.

items.title: Caliban: a from-scratch Rust agent harness
items.author: caliban-ai (GitHub)
items.summary: Caliban is a provider-agnostic Rust coding-agent harness that gives the operator control of model routing, memory, skills, permissions, MCP, and sub-agents. A readable open-source harness to compare against hosted ones.

items.title: OpenKruise Agents v0.6.0: leaping ahead in agent sandbox security and automation
items.author: CNCF (OpenKruise)
items.summary: OpenKruise Agents v0.6.0 adds traffic controls for Kubernetes agent sandboxes, including an MCP tool policy that allows or denies tools/call requests by tool name at the gateway. A per-tool allowlist enforced outside the agent.

items.title: Deutsche Bank Private Bank launches AI Academy for more than 20,000 employees
items.author: Deutsche Bank
items.summary: Deutsche Bank's Private Bank launched the PB AI Academy on Nov 5, a role-based program of self-paced courses, instructor-led sessions, workshops, and communities covering prompting, responsible use, and agents, with five to ten trainings per pathway. About 3,500 staff have access now, with rollout to more than 20,000 planned. It is a role-based curriculum design from a large bank.

items.title: NAB deploys AI for staff called 'Ruby' that is built on Anthropic
items.author: iTnews
items.summary: National Australia Bank rolled out Ruby, an internal assistant built on Anthropic, to more than 40,000 staff and set up about 50 business-led AI squads with Anthropic and AWS to build use cases such as faster credit memos and loan approvals. It pairs a company-wide tool with small squads that own specific workflows.

items.title: AI gains ground at JP Morgan, but returns remain elusive
items.author: Paperjam
items.summary: Paperjam reports that usage of Spectrum IQ at J.P. Morgan Asset Management rose fivefold in 2026 to about 750 weekly users, roughly 70-80% of the relevant investment staff, while measurable returns are still unclear. A usage-versus-value data point from a large asset manager.

items.title: Lenovo's AI adoption and change management model helps drive 36% higher daily Copilot use
items.author: Lenovo
items.summary: Lenovo says a cohort that got Copilot plus role-specific guidance, tailored training, manager involvement, and feedback used it daily at a 91% rate, against 67% for a license-only cohort. It is a controlled comparison showing training and managers matter more than licenses.

items.title: Franklin Templeton uses OpenAI to support investment research
items.author: OpenAI
items.summary: OpenAI's case study describes Franklin Templeton's network of investment AI champions turning Codex hackathon experiments into production research workflows with security review and data controls, plus hands-on labs. It is a champions-network model tied to a specific workflow.

items.title: KPMG AI Quarterly Pulse Survey, Q3 2026: asset management and private equity
items.author: KPMG
items.summary: KPMG's Q3 survey of 100 U.S. asset management and private equity leaders says 81% report measurable AI value, agent deployment rose to 30% from 19%, and data readiness is the top barrier at 76%, with 75% requiring human oversight for sensitive data. Benchmarks for where finance peers are on agents.

items.title: Grok Bot token-efficiency fixes and a one-time weekly usage reset
items.author: GrokShelf, reporting posts by xAI and Elon Musk
items.summary: After complaints that usage allowances were draining fast, xAI said on Nov 8 that token-efficiency fixes to model routing and the bot harness and routines were underway, and reset weekly limits for all users on Nov 9. The reset was one-time, not a higher allowance. It bears directly on how many routines a set of bots can run in a week.

items.title: Grok Bot can now place phone calls
items.author: Grok Bot (xAI) on X
items.summary: On Nov 4 the official Grok Bot account announced phone calls: the bot asks for approval before dialing, shows a live transcript, and lets you take over or end the call. Calls are limited to U.S. numbers and identify themselves as a virtual assistant. It adds a new outbound channel that needs the same approval discipline as email.

items.title: Grok Bot browser blocked from loopback (127.0.0.1) since Nov 6
items.author: Cursor community forum thread
items.summary: Users reported that since Nov 6 the bot's browser could not reach services on 127.0.0.1 inside its own computer while the shell still could, after a security change. The thread later says the block was fixed and that updating the bot's computer restores localhost access. It explains a class of failures for bots that test local web apps.

items.title: Grok Bot usage limit reached? 93% of my tokens were re-reading
items.author: Roshel Perera
items.summary: Roshel Perera says his roughly 60 bots used 4.6 billion tokens in a week and 93.2% went to re-reading old chat history, not replies or new prompts. He cut one bot's per-step cost from about 83-94k to 44k tokens with a short handoff file, fresh bot copies, and fewer schedules. It is a measured account of where bot tokens actually go.

items.title: Agentforce Coworker surpasses 185,000 users
items.author: Salesforce
items.summary: Salesforce says more than 185,000 users now use Agentforce Coworker, an assistant that plans and coordinates Salesforce agents and workflows, with usage up 21 times in three months. It is one of the largest reported deployments of a workplace agent assistant.

items.title: Introducing MAIA: AI that makes teams better together
items.author: Zyphra
items.summary: Zyphra opened a beta of MAIA, a personal and team agent that runs as a Mac app and in Slack, remembers work context, and acts across connected tools such as Google Workspace. It is free during beta with daily caps. Another Slack-native assistant competing in the same space as Grok Bot.

items.title: Shattering silos with OpenClaw Multiplayer
items.author: OpenClaw
items.summary: OpenClaw Multiplayer lets a trusted team share one agent and its sessions, with roles, ownership, participant history, live presence, and configurable steering modes. OpenClaw's docs say it is not an isolation layer for untrusted users. It shows how an open-source assistant handles shared bots for a team.

items.title: To innovate faster, BNY upskills 100% of staff on Eliza, powered by Microsoft AI
items.author: Microsoft Customer Stories (BNY)
items.summary: BNY says it has trained all of its roughly 50,000 employees on Eliza, its in-house AI platform built on Microsoft Azure and Foundry, through more than 400,000 hours of tiered training, and that about half of staff are building their own agents. It is a reference case for company-wide training at a large regulated financial firm.

items.title: How bottom-line focused financial firms are finding ROI in AI
items.author: Fortune
items.summary: Fortune's Sept 29 report collects bank ROI numbers: Wells Fargo says AI support lifted branch product sales 31%, Bank of America says about 140 use cases cost $400 million and returned $800 million, and JPMorgan says about $2 billion of AI investment was matched by similar benefits. These are the figures leadership teams cite when asking what AI rollout should return.

items.title: Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence: final report
items.author: Financial Stability Board
items.summary: On Oct 15 the FSB published 12 non-binding practices for financial institutions covering board oversight, accountability, risk documentation, data governance, explainability, monitoring, human oversight, cyber risk, and third-party AI risk. It is the global regulator baseline that financial firms' AI programs will be measured against.

items.title: CIO Pulse Survey: enterprise AI readiness insights
items.author: Accenture
items.summary: Accenture's Nov 3 survey of 300 technology leaders says 64% are scaling AI but only 7% optimize at scale, 70% use it mainly for individual productivity versus 37% for end-to-end agent workflows, and governance, data readiness, and training are the top barriers. It quantifies the gap between handing out tools and changing workflows.

items.title: JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs underscore security in AI plans
items.author: CIO Dive
items.summary: At Evident's Oct 22 symposium, JPMorgan CIO Lori Beer said the bank enforces 15 agent controls including identity and access management, guardrails, and evaluations, and Goldman CIO Marco Argenti said agents must be contained with zero-trust-style controls and gates before transactions. It shows how two large banks frame agent rollout around controls.

items.title: Advancing AI fluency at Capital One
items.author: Capital One Tech
items.summary: Capital One describes an enterprise AI learning hub for more than 60,000 associates, running from basic AI literacy to advanced agentic coding programs, with dedicated time set aside for experimentation. It is a model for tiered fluency training with protected time.

items.title: Teammates are agents for complex, ongoing work
items.author: Perplexity
items.summary: On Nov 4 Perplexity launched Teammates, always-on agents built on Perplexity Computer that own ongoing projects, monitor connected tools, follow up on their own, and coordinate with other teammates and with people in Slack. The research preview is for individual Max subscribers on the web. It is a direct competitor to running a set of Grok Bot agents for ongoing work.

items.title: Grok Bot changelog: 0.78 releases
items.author: xAI
items.summary: xAI's 0.78 releases added shopping product cards and order tracking, Shop Pay in the Vault, subscription templates, cloud agents in custom modes, and Team Bot login sharing, followed by subscription refund requests and smoother checkout in 0.78.4. These change what bots can buy and which logins a Team Bot can use on everyone's behalf.

items.title: Introducing OpenTeam: an open-source Grok Bot alternative
items.author: Raghav Pillai (OpenTeam)
items.summary: OpenTeam is a GPL-3.0, self-hosted take on Grok Bot that runs a team of bots in Docker, each with a persistent Linux desktop, shared workspace, memory, group chats, and routines, on any model provider. Its authors say its tools, prompt, and skills are built for compatibility with Grok Bot's. It is a reference point if you ever need bots running on hardware you control.

items.title: Put Claude to work on your computer (Dispatch and computer use)
items.author: Anthropic
items.summary: Anthropic's guide describes Dispatch, which lets you message Claude from your phone and have it work on your desktop with your files, connectors, and apps, including computer use on macOS and Windows. The desktop has to stay awake with Claude Desktop open. It shows how Anthropic is handling the same phone-to-desktop handoff that Grok Bot handles with its own box.

items.title: Introducing Pivra Desk: AI teammates on your own computer that ask before they act
items.author: Pivra
items.summary: Pivra Desk is a local-first agent for Mac and Windows that reads files and uses apps on its own but holds every send, publish, payment, or change on an approval card, with Touch ID or a typed phrase for critical actions and plain-language "never" rules. It is a concrete design for approval gates on a desktop agent.

items.title: Grok Bot skills vs routines: what to save and when
items.author: Grok Bot Wiki
items.summary: The guide separates a skill, reusable instructions for how to do a task that can be shared across bots, from a routine, which belongs to one bot and sets when the task runs. It recommends building and testing the skill first and only then scheduling it. That matches how the beat routines and vault skills are set up.

items.title: The harness and memory architecture behind self-updating docs
items.author: Mintlify
items.summary: Mintlify describes a background agent that tunes triggers, skills, and shared memory daily, runner agents that execute triggered skills and open docs PRs, and memory kept as fixed-schema JSON files in a Git repo. Mintlify says the redesign raised internal PR acceptance from 70% to 90%. A production harness with memory under version control.

items.title: Learning by Doing: Autonomously Compiling and Curating Agent Skills from Verified Traces
items.author: Daniel Chalef et al. (Zep)
items.summary: Zep describes Zep Agent Skills, a production service that turns verified agent runs into reusable skills, giving deployed agents procedural memory alongside facts and episodes. It is a worked method for bots that write their own skills from what succeeded.

items.title: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World
items.author: Ruiyao Xu et al.
items.summary: The paper uses recursive self-improvement to evolve agent harnesses for open-world tasks that were not seen when the harness was designed. It is research on letting agents rewrite their own harness safely.

items.title: How Agent Skills Evolve: A Large-Scale Empirical Study of Skills on GitHub
items.author: Jinjun Huang et al.
items.summary: The authors studied 84,200 agent skills and 750,898 commits on GitHub and built taxonomies of skill components and the changes people make to them. It shows how skills are actually maintained over time.

items.title: Just-in-Time Skill Retrieval via Long-Horizon State Tracking
items.author: Xin Lin et al.
items.summary: The paper argues that picking a fixed skill set before a long task starts fails, and retrieves skills during execution based on tracked task state instead. Relevant to how bots with many skills decide which to load.

items.title: Decision-grade intelligence everywhere: introducing SuperAnalyst MCP
items.author: AlphaSense
items.summary: AlphaSense launched SuperAnalyst MCP on Nov 4, a single MCP server that lets an outside agent delegate research and analysis to AlphaSense's own agent and get back cited answers or workbooks drawn from more than 500 million documents. It is an example of a vendor exposing a whole agent, not raw tools, over MCP.

items.title: MemCurrent: designing persistent memory for production agents
items.author: Databricks
items.summary: Databricks describes MemCurrent, the design behind its Agent Memory beta: managed sessions, a durable memory store for facts, preferences, and workflows, and background pipelines that distill sessions, remove duplicates, and resolve contradictions. A production memory architecture from a large platform vendor.

items.title: Introducing Strands Box: AI agent sandboxes powered by Dogwood
items.author: AWS Open Source Blog
items.summary: AWS released Strands Box in preview on Oct 7, an Apache-2.0 sandbox that works with any harness and pairs OS isolation with Dogwood policies controlling shell, Python, MCP, file, and network actions, where forbid rules override permits. It is a policy layer for what an agent may do inside its box.

items.title: Sandbox Agents (OpenAI Agents SDK guide)
items.author: OpenAI
items.summary: OpenAI's guide separates the harness, which owns the agent loop, tool routing, approvals, tracing, and secrets, from sandbox compute, where files, commands, and ports live, and recommends keeping credentials outside the sandbox. It is a clear statement of where the trust boundary sits in an agent.

items.title: Using agent memory (Claude Managed Agents memory stores)
items.author: Anthropic
items.summary: Anthropic's docs describe memory stores for Managed Agents: workspace-scoped collections of text documents mounted into a session, up to eight per session, with every change saved as an immutable, redactable version. Versioned memory gives an audit trail for what an agent remembered.

items.title: Build agents your way: Parloa's Agent Management API, SDK, CLI, and MCP
items.author: Parloa
items.summary: Parloa's Nov 2 release lets builders review, edit, test, and compare agent versions from Claude Code, Cursor, or ChatGPT over MCP, read-only by default, with changes saved as drafts and publishing kept as a separate controlled step. A pattern for managing agents with coding agents while keeping deployment gated.
